ambient.rule: Applied to EVERY shot that is not a hard-held detail. Amplitude is deliberately tiny — if you notice it, it is too much.

layers.motion: irregular, 1–3px lateral drift, never a loop
layers.where: every interior shot with a lamp in frame — which is almost all of arc 7
layers.note: The single highest-value effect in the product. One moving flame makes a whole still frame live.

layers.motion: 1–2 seconds of decay after any body movement, then still
layers.where: after the king stands, after he joins his hands, after the sage turns
layers.note: Uncut cloth has weight. It keeps moving after the person stops. Nothing says 'handloom' like this.

layers.motion: slow, near-random, drifting across the beam
layers.where: any shot with a lattice shaft — the sabhā, the gate, the road
layers.note: Makes light volumetric without god rays. The honest version of the thing we forbid.

layers.motion: one slow breath across a held shot
layers.where: every hold longer than 3 seconds on a person
layers.note: The 8-second hold on Daśaratha lives or dies on this. Without it he is a photograph.

layers.what: a blink, or the eyes moving
layers.motion: at most one blink in an 8-second hold; never on the beat
layers.note: One blink, late. Two reads as animation.

motivated.rule: Only when something in the scene causes it, and only where the source or our staging puts it. Never added for texture.

list.what: a thin thread of smoke from a wick
list.when: a lamp is close in frame
the rite is SHOWN — which in arc 7 is never. Spoken of only.
bare feet on packed earth — the road films
the forest films only. Dry deciduous, not a shower of falling leaves.
list.note: Leaves moving in wind, not leaves falling. Falling leaves are autumn and autumn is a European register.

list.when: the honouring in M1, and the Sarayū
the dry forest at midday only

M3.note: FX-CLOTH is essential at the beat where he stands — the cloth falling is how the audience registers that a king has come down off a dais.

M4.note: On the high wide, FX-DUST in the lattice shafts is what gives the hall its true size. The scale is in the air, not in the cut.

M5.note: NOTHING on the staff strike. The frame is absolutely still. That stillness is the effect.

M6.note: The final hold is an empty doorway with dust in the light and nothing else. Let it drift for four seconds.

M7.note: First exterior. FX-DUST-FEET on the road is where the world stops being a room.

spectacle: magical glow on a person or object
forbidden.why: Every one of these tells the audience how to feel. This arc's whole method is to state a fact and let them feel it themselves. An effect that editorialises is a lie in a different medium.
forbidden.the_test: If the effect exists to make a moment feel bigger, cut it. If it exists because a real room would do that, keep it.

earth_shaking.textual: The spine says the earth trembled when the sage was angered — ⟨Bāla 20.4, GRETIL — text withheld⟩, Bāla 20.4.
earth_shaking.our_staging: ONE strike of wood on sandstone. Dry, close, un-reverbed, 4 dB above anything else in the arc. The frame does not move.
earth_shaking.why: A shaking camera makes the audience feel the equipment. A single hard sound in a quiet room makes them feel the man. We have spent five films earning silence; spending it on a rumble would be the worst trade in the product.
earth_shaking.declared: This is our staging, not the text's instruction. The text says the earth shook. We chose to render that as a sound. Ask says so when asked.

rejection_criteria: the camera moves when the shot is marked locked
